    Perform multi-group statistical testing

    test_multi_groups.Rd

    The test_multi_groups function performs a statistical comparison of multiple groups using either parametric or non-parametric methods, depending on the data and user preference. It includes Levene's test for variance homogeneity, followed by one of: ANOVA, Welch's ANOVA, or Kruskal-Wallis test. Post-hoc pairwise comparisons are also performed without p-value adjustment.

    test_multi_groups(
  df,
  value_column,
  grouping_column,
  parametric = TRUE,
  adjustment.method = "bonferroni"
)

    Arguments

    df

    A data frame containing the input data.

    value_column

    A string specifying the name of the numeric column with values to test.

    grouping_column

    A string specifying the name of the column with grouping information.

    parametric

    Logical. If TRUE, parametric tests (ANOVA or Welch’s ANOVA) are used. If FALSE, the Kruskal-Wallis test is used.

    adjustment.method

    A string indicating the method for p-value adjustment (currently stored in the output but not applied during post-hoc tests; default is "bonferroni").

    Value

    An S4 object of class statistic with the following slots:

    • test — name of the main statistical test used ("ANOVA", "Welch's ANOVA", or "Kruskal-Wallis"),

    • leven_var_test — a list with results from Levene’s test and interpretation,

    • posthoc_test — name of the post-hoc test performed,

    • test_data — a list containing the main test statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value,

    • posthoc_data — a list containing raw p-values and group comparisons from post-hoc tests.

    Details

    - If parametric = FALSE, Kruskal-Wallis and pairwise Wilcoxon tests are used. - If parametric = TRUE, Levene’s test is used to choose between:

    • Equal variances → classical ANOVA and pairwise t-tests,

    • Unequal variances → Welch’s ANOVA and Welch t-tests.

    - P-values in post-hoc tests are returned unadjusted but can be manually corrected later using adjustment.method.

    This function is primarily used internally by multi_groups_analysis to encapsulate statistical logic.

    Examples

    df <- data.frame(
  group = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 10),
  value = c(rnorm(10, mean = 5), rnorm(10, mean = 6), rnorm(10, mean = 7))
)
test_multi_groups(df, value_column = "value", grouping_column = "group", parametric = TRUE)
